_declaration_of_independence_from_fixtur: Each rule below states a GENERAL commercial requirement for the parameter type, expressed as a deterministic computation over the panel's returned classification fields.
No rule references a fixture, a lease, a candidate id, a document value, or an expected outcome.
No rule contains a lease literal (no percentage, no dollar figure, no clause number, no party name).

The reviewer test (§4): can you tell each requirement apart from the outcome we expect on the seeded candidates? If a requirement can only be justified by pointing at what cand_0N should produce, it is an answer key in schema form and is WRONG.
These profiles are compared against the panel's output by CODE, AFTER blind classification (Part A §4.2 part 2). They are never shown to a model.

operators.set_equals: returned set equals the literal set exactly (order-insensitive, duplicate-insensitive)
operators.set_contains: every member of the literal set is present in the returned set; additional members are permitted and are preserved as semantic identity
operators.in: scalar membership in a literal list
operators.is_non_empty_set: returned set has >= 1 member and is not 'none'/'unclear'/'not_applicable'
operators.field: read a named field from the merged candidate_semantic_result
operators.deterministic: read a code-computed deterministic check, not a model field

_evaluation_semantics.tri_state_rule: Any operand whose underlying field is 'unclear', 'not_assessable', or was invalidated by field-grounding failure (Part A §4.5) evaluates the predicate to 'undeterminable', NEVER to false. undeterminable never yields a match and never yields a terminal negative.
_evaluation_semantics.not_applicable_rule: 'not_applicable' is a schema-fixed value meaning the dimension is not a meaningful attribute of this parameter. It is NOT 'none' and NOT 'unclear', and it satisfies a requirement that declares it.

tenant_share._requirement_in_one_line: A tenant's share parameter must state a tenant's proportional share that applies to OPERATING EXPENSES, as an operative contractual term carrying its own percentage.
tenant_share._why_this_is_the_general_requirement_not: The ratified parameter is defined as "Tenant's Share of Operating Expenses percentage" (PARAMETER_TARGETS, cam/adapters/lease_review/lease_parameter_block.py). That definition requires the percentage to apply to operating expenses; it does NOT state that it must apply ONLY to operating expenses. A share whose grounded basis does not include operating expenses at all is a different commercial quantity and does not satisfy a dependency declared for operating-expense exposure. Requiring exclusivity would add a condition the ratified definition never states.

basis_match.rule: match iff "operating_expenses" is a MEMBER of the grounded value_applies_to_charge_basis_components set (inclusion, not exact equality)

computation.mismatch: a returned set that is fully determined and does NOT contain operating_expenses
computation.undeterminable: value_applies_to_charge_basis_components is unclear, DISPUTED, none, or invalidated by field-grounding failure — never false, never a terminal negative

basis_match._additional_components_note: Additional grounded components (e.g. taxes, CAM, insurance) are PRESERVED as part of the candidate's semantic identity and do NOT independently cause mismatch. A single combined percentage that applies to operating expenses among other charge bases still applies to operating expenses.
basis_match._relation_bearing_note: v3.3: the field this operates on, value_applies_to_charge_basis_components, carries ONLY the bases this candidate's OWN value applies to (established by cited value-to-basis linkage), NOT bases merely co-mentioned in context and NOT bases governed by a different value expression. Membership in this field is therefore 'the value applies to operating_expenses', a checkable claim — not 'operating_expenses appears near the value', a co-location artifact. A candidate whose value-to-basis linkage is not citation-grounded has its field invalidated by §4.5 grounding failure and routes to undeterminable (never match).
basis_match._amendment: v3.1 -> v3.2 changed this predicate from set_equals to set_contains. v3.3 renamed the underlying field to the relation-bearing value_applies_to_charge_basis_components (from the pre-v3.3 co-occurrence field name) to close the co-occurrence-false-match defect (blind Review B + GPT informed audit); the set_contains predicate is unchanged, only the field it reads is now relation-bearing. Scoped to tenant_share. The error-profile accounting lives in the v3.2.1/v3.3 Amendment Records, NOT here — this profile states the requirement, not the measurement's expected outcomes.

charge_scope.rule: RECORDED AS METADATA ONLY — does NOT gate qualification in v1
charge_scope._explicit_note: Stated explicitly rather than left silently either-way (§4). Scope (building vs project vs premises) is captured for observation but no v1 requirement turns on it.

text_role_ok._why: A parameter dependency must be satisfied by a term that operates, not by a definition that points elsewhere or a narrative description of one.

value_ok.rule: value_completeness is self_contained AND the deterministic value-token check passes on this same candidate
value_ok._why: A share parameter that does not carry its own figure has not supplied the quantity the dependent provision needs.

relevance_ok.rule: parameter_family_relevance equals relevant, unanimously across the panel
relevance_ok._why: Part A §5.1/§6.3: minority relevance RETAINS evidence but does not CERTIFY.

applicability_match.rule: applicable iff the candidate's identity/support fit the share concept — INDEPENDENT of whether it carries a value
applicability_match._why: Part A §6.2: requiring value_ok for applicability is the circularity the review forbade. A candidate may establish that a share mechanism APPLIES in this document while being not_qualified to SATISFY the parameter.
applicability_match.not_applicable_requires: completeness_provenance.status == established — otherwise a negative is not_assessable, never not_applicable

building_share._status: DECLARED BUT UNEXERCISED — no candidate is seeded for this parameter (§6.1). Profile present so the parameter set is complete and the omission is visible rather than silent.
building_share._requirement_in_one_line: A building's share parameter must state the building's proportional share of PROJECT operating expenses as an operative contractual term carrying its own percentage.

charge_scope.rule: RECORDED AS METADATA ONLY — does NOT gate qualification in v1

base_rent._requirement_in_one_line: A base rent parameter must be an operative rent term that carries its own rent figure, not a definition that cross-references the figure elsewhere.
base_rent._why_this_is_the_general_requirement_not: A downstream provision depending on base rent needs the amount. A definitional stub naming the term while pointing to another section has not supplied it — this is true of any lease drafted with a definitions article, and would equally disqualify a stub in the lease the block was built on.

basis_match.rule: not_applicable — charge basis is not a meaningful attribute of base rent
basis_match._note: Per Part A §4.1. Because this is schema-fixed, the field is exempt from the §4.5 field_support grounding requirement.

text_role_ok._why: A definition role, by itself, does not operate to fix the rent.

value_ok.rule: value_completeness is self_contained AND the deterministic value-token check passes on this same candidate
value_ok._consequence: A candidate classified cross_reference_only or no_value fails this predicate and is not_qualified. This follows from the rule; it is not a per-candidate expectation.

applicability_match.rule: applicable iff a candidate's text_role names/establishes the base-rent concept as a term of this lease — INDEPENDENT of whether it carries a value
applicability_match._why: Part A §6.2 worked example: a definition stub CAN establish that a base-rent mechanism applies in this lease (positive applicability) while being not_qualified to satisfy the parameter. Excluding 'definition' here would recreate the circularity.

rent_adjustment_pct._requirement_in_one_line: A rent adjustment parameter must be an operative escalation term carrying its own rate, not a narrative description of a schedule.
rent_adjustment_pct._why_this_is_the_general_requirement_not: A contractual escalation rate binds; a sentence describing what a schedule approximately reflects does not create the obligation and may be an inexact summary of it. The distinction between an operative rate and a descriptive aside is a general drafting distinction, not a property of any one document.

basis_match.rule: not_applicable — charge basis is not a meaningful attribute of a rent adjustment rate
basis_match._note: Per Part A §4.1. Schema-fixed, therefore exempt from the §4.5 grounding requirement.

text_role_ok._consequence: A candidate classified narrative fails this predicate. This is the case-4 discriminator ENCODED AS A RULE about drafting, not as an expected outcome for any candidate.

value_ok.rule: value_completeness is self_contained AND the deterministic value-token check passes on this same candidate

applicability_match.rule: applicable iff a candidate establishes a rent-adjustment mechanism as a term of this lease — INDEPENDENT of whether it carries a value

_qualification_rule.candidate_qualification: qualified iff relevance_ok AND basis_match in {match, not_applicable} AND text_role_ok AND value_ok AND support_ok — ALL evaluated on the SAME candidate
_qualification_rule.certification: satisfied iff SOME SINGLE candidate is qualified AND applicability_match == applicable; otherwise the outcome is a review_needed_* state per the certification policy
_qualification_rule.terminal_negative_gate: no unsatisfied_* state may be emitted unless completeness_provenance.status == established (this measurement sets not_established, so none may be emitted)
